record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let X be the space of continuous actions of the free group F2 on two generators. Is the collection of actions that are measure isomorphic to Bernoulli F2-actions a Borel set?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1 (Foreman). Let X be the space of continuous actions of the free group F2 on two generators. Is the collection of Bernoulli actions measure isomorphic to Bernoulli F2-actions a Borel set? (Borel actions?)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F_2$ denote the free group on two generators. Let $X$ be the Polish space of continuous actions of $F_2$ on the Cantor space (equivalently, the space of pairs of homeomorphisms of the Cantor space, with the topology inherited from the homeomorphism group). For each action $\alpha \in X$ and each $\alpha$-invariant Borel probability measure, one obtains a measure-preserving action of $F_2$ on a standard probability space. Call an action $\alpha \in X$ "Bernoulli-isomorphic" if there exists an $\alpha$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ such that the measure-preserving system $(\alpha, \mu)$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to some Bernoulli shift action of $F_2$ on a standard probability space $(K^{F_2}, \nu^{F_2})$.

Question: Is the set of Bernoulli-isomorphic actions a Borel subset of $X$? (Same question with "Borel" weakened to other natural pointclasses, e.g. is it the image of a Borel function?)

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not turn up a published resolution of Foreman's question on the Borel complexity of the set of continuous F_2-actions measure-isomorphic to Bernoulli actions. Related work (Foreman–Rudolph–Weiss on the non-Borelness of measure isomorphism for Z-actions, and Bowen's work on Bernoulli shifts of free groups) is well known, but the specific F_2 descriptive-complexity question appears to still be open.

status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to investigate the descriptive complexity of measure-isomorphism for group actions without resolving this specific Borelness question for Bernoulli F_2-actions.
